newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crude grades accelerate gains, outrights weak.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crude grades accelerate gains, outrights weak.

text.p: U.S. domestic crude grades gathered steam in Tuesday afternoon trade, selling at firmer differentials to the weakening March West Texas Intermediate/Cushing benchmark.
Outright prices failed to move out of established trading ranges, pressured by a seasonal price retreat based on technical and fundamental factors.
An oil workers strike in Colombia left the markets bored, despite union goals to cut production by 50 percent.
March WTI/Cushing was currently around 15 cents lower at $22.30-40 a barrel, and Mar/Apr spreads at 25 cts.
On the grade side of business, traders said Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sold between a 25-29 cts premium to the WTI/Cushing, 5-8 cts higher than Monday deals.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was sold at a 20 cts discount to the WTI/Cushing, around 10 cts firmer than last deals.
Midland/WTI remained the quiet market in an increasingly busy session, talking at a 36-39 cts discount.
West Texas Sour/Midland sold between a $2.10-15 discount to the marker, also firming along with the sweet grades.
A combination of more expensive foreign barrels and heightened refiner demand bolstered the grades, traders said.
Other deals were confirmed for Mar Postings Plus at $2.04, and for the Eugene Island sour at negative $2.20 to the WTI.
